entries.german:
Vidimus der beiden Urkunden dd. Goldenkron, 1. Mai 1481 und vom 25. Juni desselben Jahres.(N. CCXXXIII und CCXXXIV.)

Nos Thomas abbas monasterii Altivadensis ordinis Cisterciensis Pragensis diocesis tenore praesentium universis et singulis recognoscimus et profitemur, quod venerabilis in Christo pater et dominus dominus Conradus abbas Sanctae Coronae ad praesentiam nostram veniens, habens et tenens duas litteras in pargameno suae electionis et absolutionis a professione, maiorem cum tribus sigillis, minorem cum uno sigillo pendentibus et easdem in praesentia nostra in medium et coram produxit, quarum quidem litterarum effectus et tenores de verbo ad verbum sequuntur et sunt tales: (Folgt der Wortlaut oben bezeichneter Urkunden.) Visis itaque eisdem litteris, salvis, integris, non cancellatis nec rasis, sed inviolatis et per nos diligenter perlectis et auscultatis, petiit dictus venerabilis pater et dominus dominus abbas Sanctae Coronae instanter, instantius, instantissime, sibi per nos earundem litterarum vidimus et transscriptum fieri. Nos eius precibus victi ipsas litteras sic de verbo ad verbum nichil in eisdem addicientes neque minuentes, quod sensum variare videtur aut mutare intellectum, per omnia inscribere, sollicite collationari et in hanc litteram ,Vidimus‘ redigere fecimus, addicientes insuper et decernentes, ut ipsa littera ,Vidimus‘ eandem vim, ubicunque totiens et quotiens oportunum fuerit, habeat et habere debeat cew litterae originales. In cuius rei testimonium praesentes litteras fieri, sigillique nostri pendentis robore iussimus communiri. Datum et actum in monasterio nostro Altivadensi decimo octavo die mensis Octobris, anni domini millesimi quadringentesimi octogesimi primi. Testes huius rei sunt venerabilis pater frater Jacobus prior, frater Thomas cellerarius dicti monasterii, dominus Nicolaus plebanus in Altovado et dominus Martinus pannificis de Rosenberg Wiennensis bonarum artium liberalium baccalaureus, tunc temporis divinorum cooperator eiusdem opidi, specialiter ad praemissa vocati et petiti.
entries.english:
Certified copy of the two charters dated at Goldenkron on 1 May 1481 and 25 June of the same year (Nos. CCXXXIII and CCXXXIV).

We, Thomas, abbot of the Cistercian monastery of Altovado in the diocese of Prague, hereby acknowledge and declare to all and each that the venerable father in Christ and lord, Lord Conrad, abbot of Sancta Corona, came before us, bearing and holding two parchment letters concerning his election and absolution from his profession: the larger with three pendant seals and the smaller with one. He produced them there in our presence, and the effect and wording of those letters follow word for word as set out below (the wording of the above-mentioned letters follows).

Having seen these letters, which were sound, intact, neither cancelled nor scraped, but untouched, and having carefully read and heard them, the said venerable father and lord, the abbot of Sancta Corona, earnestly, more earnestly, and most earnestly requested that we make him a certified copy and transcript of those letters. Moved by his entreaties, we caused those letters to be copied carefully, word for word, adding nothing and removing nothing that might alter their sense or change their meaning, collated in every respect, and set down in this instrument of certification. We further added and decreed that this instrument of certification shall have, and shall continue to have, the same force wherever and whenever required as the original letters. In witness of this, we ordered that this instrument be made and secured with the authority of our pendant seal. Given and done at our monastery of Altovado on the eighteenth day of October in the year of Our Lord 1481. Witnesses to this matter are the venerable father Brother Jacob, prior; Brother Thomas, cellarer of the said monastery; Lord Nicolaus, parish priest at Altovado; and Lord Martin Pannificis of Rosenberg, bachelor of liberal arts at Vienna and at that time assistant in divine services in the same town, specially summoned and requested for the foregoing.
